en: Case it. Plan it. Take it.
The heist keeps running while this menu is open. You stand still until you resume.
Leave the game? Unsecured loot stays behind.
One down before custody. Higher stakes, same pay.
No restarts. Fail and the contract is gone.
Fill empty slots with crew AI
None yet: buy and equip one in the Workshop
Hold on: your crew can revive you
Trade the marked hostage to free your crew
Unlocked doors open while casing. Locks and anything suspicious need the mask.
Walk in like you belong. Unmasked, nobody minds you.
Find the guards, the cameras and the way to the loot.
Unlocked doors are fine. Locks and loot need the mask.
Hold to mask up. It stays on.
Guards and cameras spot you over time. A ring over them fills, and "!" means you are seen.
Answer a downed guard's pager fast, or the alarm goes off.
Guards and cameras can see you through clear glass.
Interact: doors, loot, pagers, cable ties.
Throw a carried bag. Heavy ones slow you down.
The police assault in waves. Move in the lulls.
Shout civilians down and tie them. Hostages buy time.
Keep moving the loot to the secure zone.
The getaway is here. Head for the escape zone.
Unsecured bags pay nothing. Go now or grab more.
You leave when the whole crew is in the zone.
The safe opens with the manager's keycard or the safe code. Without either, it takes a slow, quiet lockpick.
The keycard could be anywhere. The code is on a note.
Swipe the card or enter the code: quick and quiet.
A drill opens it too, but it's loud. The floor guard hears it.
The vault needs the keycard and the time-lock code, or the server-room hack.
The code starts the time lock. Keep the basement quiet until it opens.
Lasers guard the panel. Find the gap, time the sweep, or cross when the grid drops.
The cage opens with its code (find the note) or the saw.
The saw is a last resort: the camera operator sits through the wall.
The array resyncs and stops the hack. Interact to keep it running.
One alarm and the job is over.
Carry the thermite bag to the product and place it on the burn point.
It burns 30 s, then fire shutters close the room. Don't be inside.
Pick or saw the lock to open a container. The rifles are behind the Co-op's brass padlocks; a customs seal alone means empty.
Only the listed canvases count. The Lantern Bearer is a must.
Cut a canvas from the stretcher, then carry it rolled.
Until last call, you can walk the ground floor unmasked as a guest.
At last call the guests leave, and the whole building is restricted.
Rig the junction signals before the convoy comes: it stops clean at the red light, and you get 8 s before the escort reacts.
Without the signals, Reyes rams it with the mixer and the fight starts at once. An early alarm also locks the trucks down.
Saw or blow open the trucks. The bullion truck's rear doors need the thermite bag.
Secure at least 4 bags before the escape. Gold is heavy.
Ashgrove, the day manager, carries the vault keycard. Take it from him.
Hack the right officer's computer, or the server rack, for the vault code. It starts a long time lock.
Go loud and the vault locks down: call in the thermal drill and burn through from the teller floor.
Bags go up the hoist. Nobody climbs the ladder carrying one.
You walk in as a guest, with no mask and no gear. Look around freely: you need the insider's bag before you can mask up.
Crale's office takes a keycard. The staff keep one somewhere in the club.
Find the combination and the safe opens in seconds. Without it, drill it: slower, and it jams.
Three bags of the safe's cash call the van. Go loud and the crowd stampedes for the doors.

The whole crew ended up in custody.
The alarm went off on a stealth-only job.
The crew walked away from the job.
Payout if you had made it

Clean job. Nobody knew we were there.
Quiet job. Not a clean one.

A compact nine-millimetre service pistol. Light, quiet to carry, forgiving to learn.
Lacquered gold over a long, patient face. It has seen worse jobs than yours.
Cold white glaze, hairline cracks, no expression at all. It keeps watch so you don't have to.
Sea-green scales on a sly fox face. Slippery in every sense.
An owl wired for the night shift. Only turns up in a payday hand.
Hazard yellow and soot stripes on a jaw built for doors.
Dark lacquer and a brass sunrise. Earned by crews who finish what others only start.
Printed like a cheap poster, smiling like it knows the vault code.
Turns gunfire into a polite cough. Heavier at the muzzle and a little less punch.
A red dot for quicker shots on target. Adds bulk under a jacket.
More rounds between reloads. Sticks out of the grip, slows the swap.
Small, quiet and always in the pocket.
A double-edged dagger with a weighted pommel. Quick and quiet.
A sharpened toothbrush. It hits harder than it looks when charged.
Snaps out to full length with a flick. Light, and good at putting people on the floor.
A batting-cage favourite. Long reach and a big charged swing.
From the toolbox in the van. Short, heavy and reliable.
A length of old plumbing. Slow to bring round, hard to stand up after.
Six kilos on a long handle. Heavy to carry, devastating when charged.
A long jungle blade with a good reach.
Taken off a wall marked IN CASE OF EMERGENCY. This is one.
A butcher's cleaver. Short, broad and heavy at the edge.
No armor, all elegance. Nobody looks twice at a good suit.
Thin ballistic panels that vanish under a coat.
The standard compromise between coverage and mobility.
Reinforced panels front and back. You will feel it on the stairs.
Shoulder-to-hip protection. Hard to hide, harder to put down.
Ceramic plates for people who expect a long day.
Full plate carrier for walking through the front door. Requires training to move in.
Patches the crew up and resets their downs. Two uses.
A heavy bag of spare magazines for the whole crew.
Holds three body bags for a tidy crew.
Jams cameras, pagers and phones for 20 seconds. One unit.
Four small kits; each heals one heister once.
Three mines that blow when someone crosses the beam.
An automatic turret that fires at anyone hostile in its arc. Deploying it costs 40% of your ammo.
The bot revives a downed teammate it can see from up to 9 m away by shouting, at most once every 30 seconds.
The bot interacts 30% faster: bags, doors and revives.
The bot's shouts carry 50% further when it controls civilians and guards.
While the bot is in play, the whole crew carries 25% more ammo.
While the bot is in play, the whole crew has 10% more health.
While the bot is in play, the whole crew has 25% more stamina.
While the bot is in play, the whole crew revives 20% faster.
While the bot is in play, bags slow the whole crew 25% less.
Rings, necklaces and watches in a padded bag.
Heavy and awkward. Out of sight is out of mind.
Vossberg keeps the good stones in the back and the cameras in the front. Odile wants the back.
Alright, you're in. Keep the masks in your pockets and look like you belong.
Take your time. Count the cameras, count the guards, and try to look bored.
Mask's on. No more pretending you belong here.
Faces covered. From here on, it counts.
His pager's going. Somebody pick that up and be convincing.
Pager. Answer it before his boss gets curious.
That's the last one they'll buy.
That was your last free pass. No more bodies with radios.
Too many check-ins. Dispatch knows something's wrong. Here comes the noise.
Nobody believes a fifth all-clear. They're calling it in.
Silence on the pager. They're sending company.
Someone found a body. That's going to be hard to explain.
A body's been spotted. Get ready.
You're on tape. Somebody's watching that monitor.
Drill's on. It'll take a while, so get comfortable.
Drill's stopped. Somebody give it some encouragement.
The drill's jammed again. Cheap hardware, I know.
Drill's through. Go see what we paid for.
Crew member down. Don't leave them there.
They've got one of you. We'll get them back, but finish the job first.
One in custody. I'll start working on a trade.
That's a clean exit. Drinks are on the contract.
Done. Everyone home and the money's moving.
That one's gone. We'll talk about it later.
Pull out. There's nothing left worth getting caught for.
In and out and nobody the wiser. That's how it's supposed to go.
Not a single shot fired. I'm almost impressed.
That's the alarm. This one was quiet or nothing, so we're done. Pull out.
That was the last pager they'll swallow. Keep the rest breathing.
Test run. Nothing here is real except the bullets.
Hands where I can see them! Don't you move!
Drill's stuck. Need hands on it.
We're loud. Masks on, guns up.
Hit hard. Somebody get me up.
Civilian down. That's on our tab.
Loud it is. Try to keep up.
I'm down. Not my best moment.
On your feet, I'm not carrying you.
Swapping mags. Give me a sec.
Drill's dead. Kicking it back on.
Here we go. Loud and proud.
His pager's beeping, I'm on it.
Bagging the body, gimme a second.
Can't get up, need a medic!
I got you, I got you.
Pager. I've got it, keep moving.
Leave that one to me. I'll talk to his dispatcher.
The drill's stalled. Somebody nurse it.
Drill's sulking again. Give it a hand.
Bagging him. Keep an eye out.
Body's going in the bag. Nobody saw a thing.
Right. Loud it is. Stick to the backup plan.
There goes the quiet version. Plan B, people.
I'm down. Not as young as I was.
Down here. A hand, if you please.
Up you get. We're not done.
More of them. Use the corners.
We don't shoot the help. Ever.
Pager! I got it, I got it!
On the pager. Smooth talk, coming up.
Mag out, mag in, two seconds!
Drill quit on us. Somebody restart it!
Loud now. Let's make it fast!
I'm down! Somebody pull me up!
Up, up! We've got a ride to catch.
Here comes the blue. Heads down!
Pager. Give it here, I'll sweet-talk him.
I've got the pager. Act natural.
The drill quit. Get it running.
Into the bag. Nobody saw that.
That's it, we're loud. Ride it out.
Loud, then. Let's be quick about it.
Up you get. We're not leaving you.
Got you. Back on your feet.
More of them. Watch the doors.
That's on us now. Stop it.
Leave the pager to me. Steady voice.
Drill's jammed. I'll look at it if nobody else will.
That drill's stuck again. Give it a nudge.
Bagging this one. Watch my back.
In the bag he goes. Tidy.
I'm down. Give us a hand.
Another lot coming in. Heads down.

Pair up with a teammate. Every kill either of you makes heals you both.

You get another 20% more health (40% in total).
